name: LT1468 / LT1469 / LT1468-2 / LT1469-2
tagline: Linear Tech's 16-bit-accurate op-amp for DAC I/V: 5 nV/√Hz, 90 MHz, ±15 V, ultra-low distortion; a measurement-led pick.

lineage.note: Sole source. LT1468 single c. Nov 1998; LT1469 dual c. 2000 (LT Magazine Vol 10 No 2, May 2000).
Bought Linear in 2017. Serves Linear documents with codes kept: 1469fb, 14692f, 1468fb, 14682fb.

part_numbers.note: PDIP-8; likely active. Top mark LT1469CN8/IN8; C 0–70 °C, I −40–85 °C. LCSC C663979.
SO-8; likely active. Top mark '1469' (C) or '1469I' (I). Mouser 584-LT1469CS8#TRPBF.
12-lead 4×4 mm DFN, low-offset A grade. Pad (pin 13) to V-. Mark '1469'.
12-lead DFN, standard grade (VOS 225 µV max). ADI datasheet listed under LT1469IDF#TRPBF.
Own datasheet 14692f. AV ≥ 2 only: 200 MHz, 30 V/µs, 75 µV VOS max.

part_numbers.pn: LT1468 (CN8, IN8, CS8, IS8, CDD, IDD) / LT1468A (ACDD, AIDD)
part_numbers.note: Single version, datasheet 1468fb; 75 µV VOS max per related-parts table. DD = 8-lead DFN.
Single, AV ≥ 2 only: 200 MHz, 30 V/µs. Datasheet 14682fb.

key_specs.value: 5 nV/√Hz typ (at 10 kHz; no 1 kHz value given)
90 MHz typ (60 min) ±15 V; 88 MHz (55 min) ±5 V
22 V/µs typ (15 min) ±15 V; 17 V/µs (11 min) ±5 V
THD −125 dB at 1 kHz; −96.5 dB at 100 kHz
±4.5 V min (PSRR-guaranteed; ±2.5 V typ) to 36 V abs max
4.1 mA typ / 5.2 max per amp ±15 V; 3.8 / 5.0 at ±5 V
±22 mA typ (±15 min); short-circuit ±40 mA (±25 min)
50/125 µV typ/max (N8, S8, A DF); 100/225 µV (DF)
IB− 3/±10 nA (trimmed); IB+ −10/±40 nA; IOS 13/±50 nA
Bipolar, bias-cancelled; only −IN IB trimmed; Cin 4 pF

reputation.summary: Linear calls it 'optimum' for DAC I/V and ADC buffers and shows a 0.00025% THD+N balanced line driver. diyAudio members call it as clean as the OPA627 but quieter and more neutral; one, citing Samuel Groner's shootout, rated it 'best of the bunch overall'. Others found it thin, heard 'metallic' treble, or wanted more output current.
typical_uses: I/V conversion for current-output DACs (LTC1597 example)
DAC post-filter and active reconstruction filters
ADC input buffer or driver (LTC1604 example)
Balanced line driver, paralleled with LT1364 (0.0008% 20 Hz–20 kHz)
Op-amp rolling in DAC output stages
caveats: -2 variants (LT1468-2/LT1469-2) need gain ≥ 2 and may oscillate in unity-gain sockets; check the suffix.
Layout-sensitive: ground plane, short leads, 0.01–0.1 µF plus 1–10 µF bypass; one 'metallic' report blamed bypassing.
An input within 0.5 V of V+ reverses output phase. Cap load limit 100 pF (G=1), 300 pF (G=−1).
Add CF ≥ RG·CIN/RF (DACs add tens of pF; LTC1597 example uses 15 pF/12k). Avoid balanced source resistances.
±22 mA output and 4.1 mA/amp (6.5 mA hot); needs ±4.5 V min. Old LTspice -2 symbols mislabelled 90 MHz.

counterfeit_notes: No LT1468/LT1469 fakes reported. Genuine marks: SO-8 '1469' or '1469I'; PDIP 'LT1469CN8'/'LT1469IN8'; DFN '1469'. It is pricey, so buy from authorized distributors and distrust cheap 'LT1469CN8' DIPs. Check you did not get an LT1469-2.

open_questions: What are ADI's lifecycle labels per variant, and does PCN 24_0236 record a process or silicon change?
Which mirrors hold pre-2011 LT1469 editions, and which limits changed in Rev B (EC pages 3, 5, 6)?
Dates and change logs for 1468fb, 14682fb and 14692f? When exactly was the LT1468 introduced?

Does Groner's survey PDF support the 'very low common-mode distortion' claim for the LT1469?

claims_confirmed: ADI serves the LT1469 datasheet as 1469fb.pdf; revision history begins at Rev B: https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/1469fb.pdf
LT1469-2 has a separate datasheet, 14692f, 'Dual 200MHz, 30V/µs 16-Bit Accurate AV ≥ 2 Op Amp': https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/14692f.pdf
LT1468 datasheet is 1468fb, calling it optimum for DAC I/V and ADC buffers: https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/1468fb.pdf
Front page: 16-bit accuracy, 900 ns settling to 150 µV (10 V step), 22 V/µs: https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/1469fb.pdf

Intro article appears with LT Magazine May 2000: https://www.analog.com/en/resources/technical-articles/dual-operational-amplifier-combines-16bit-precision-with-high-speed.html and https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/lt-journal-article/ltmag_v10n2_may00.pdf
Mirrors exist for LT1469 (alldatasheet 70456/257793/257814/1043925, datasheetq 452586, radiolocman 339815/525593) and LT1468: https://www.alldatasheet.com/datasheet-pdf/pdf/70456/LINER/LT1469.html
Mouser lists an Analog Devices LT1469 series: https://eu.mouser.com/c/semiconductors/amplifier-ics/?m=Analog+Devices+Inc.&series=LT1469
diyAudio: 'as clean as the OPA627 but quieter and more neutral', ~20 mA output limit, better I/V than OPA627: https://www.diyaudio.com/forums/digital-source/83291-killer-opamp.html

diyAudio: citing Groner, LT1469 'should be the best of the bunch overall'; also 'rather thin', 'metallic' treble: https://www.diyaudio.com/community/threads/best-opamp-for-i-v-conversion-dac.34324/page-12
